title: Normalized flat degree-zero tensor on the unbounded derived category
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $L$ a flat $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Use sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and its additive constraints [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], unbounded cochain complexes and their derived localization $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(R)\to D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the specified K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Set $T_L(M)=M\otimes_R L$ and $C(T_L)(C)^r=C^r\otimes_R L$, with differential $d_C^r\otimes1$. Write $L[0]$ for the complex with $L$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere.

The complex $L[0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and has flat terms. The canonical degree-zero totalization isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_RL[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}C(T_L)(C)$$
has the identity on its only nonzero summand in each degree, for every unbounded complex $C$. There is a natural isomorphism of exact functors of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$\eta_L:(-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q(L[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}D(T_L),$$
where $D(T_L)$ has the termwise factorization of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. If $\varphi_C:D(T_L)(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(T_L)C)$ is that factorization, then $\varphi_C\circ\eta_{L,QC}$ is precisely the fixed-K-flat-factor representative comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated], followed by the displayed totalization isomorphism. This is a comparison for every $C$, with no K-flatness or flat-term condition on $C$. It commutes with every integer shift; on termwise complexes the shift identification is the identity in each degree, with differential $(-1)^n(d_C\otimes1)$ for shift $[n]$. The triangulated compatibility includes the connecting morphisms of distinguished triangles.

For each $i\in\mathbf Z$ there is a natural isomorphism on $D(R)$,
$$\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q(L[0]))\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^i(K)\otimes_R L,$$
whose value on $K=QC$ is the above representative comparison followed by the exact-functor cohomology comparison induced on cycles and boundaries [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. No boundedness, constructibility, or invertibility of $L$ is assumed.

proof.text: Flatness of L means that the explicit site tensorRight functor preserves finite limits and finite colimits [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Transport these properties to the canonical monoidal tensorRight L using siteSheafTensorRightIso from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits]. The existing additive tensor instances and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] supply the additive abelian setting. If an object is zero, tensorRight by it is a zero functor, hence preserves all limits and colimits. Transport this exactness back through the same site tensor comparison to obtain flatness of every zero sheaf.

For any complex $C$, the degree-$r$ sum in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] has zero summands except $(p,q)=(r,0)$, since $L[0]^q=0$ for $q\ne0$. Projection onto that summand and its inclusion are inverse: their composites are identities on each coproduct summand. They define $\theta_C:\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R L[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}C(T_L)C$, equal to the identity on $C^r\otimes_R L$. The second tensor differential vanishes, so the remaining differential is $d_C^r\otimes1$. For a chain map $f:C\to C^{\prime}$, both induced maps on the surviving summand are $f^r\otimes1$; therefore $\theta$ is natural on all complexes. This computation involves a single possibly nonzero summand in each degree, even when $C$ is unbounded.

source.place: Section 06YL (section-flat), total tensor convention of homology.tex Definition 012Z

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the exact additive functor $T_L$. For every complex $C$ and integer $i$ it gives the natural cycle-and-boundary isomorphism $c_C^i:H^i(C(T_L)C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(C)\otimes_R L$. If $C$ is acyclic this object is $0\otimes_R L=0$. The isomorphism $\theta_C$ of step 2 then shows that $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R L[0])$ is acyclic. This is precisely K-flatness of $L[0]$ by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its terms are flat: its degree-zero term is the given $L$, and all others are the zero flat sheaf from step 1.

By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] applied to $T_L$, its termwise functor preserves all quasi-isomorphisms and descends to an exact functor $D(T_L)$, with the natural factorization $\varphi_C:D(T_L)(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(T_L)C)$. The cited theorem supplies its compatible comparisons for every integer shift, induced by the degreewise identity $C(T_L)(C[n])\cong(C(T_L)C)[n]$. Its hypotheses are satisfied by step 1; in particular no boundedness condition enters.

Put $F=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q(L[0])$. Step 3 allows [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] with fixed factor $A=L[0]$: $F$ is exact, and its natural representative comparison is $\chi_C:F(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R L[0])$ for every $C$. Form $a_C=\varphi_C^{-1}\circ Q(\theta_C)\circ\chi_C:F(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(T_L)(QC)$. These are natural on complexes. The natural-transformation part of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] extends $a$ uniquely along $Q$ to a natural isomorphism $\eta_L:F\xrightarrow{\sim}D(T_L)$; the inverse family extends too, and uniqueness makes both composites identities. By construction $\varphi_C\circ\eta_{L,QC}=Q(\theta_C)\circ\chi_C$, exactly the required normalization. The fixed-factor theorem requires K-flatness and flat terms only of $L[0]$, so this equality holds for arbitrary $C$.

source.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding fixed-factor construction); localization natural-transformation universal property

proof.text: For $n\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] says that extracting $[n]$ from the first argument of total tensor is unsigned. Specializing the second argument to $L[0]$, both paths from $\operatorname{Tot}(C[n]\otimes_R L[0])$ to $(C(T_L)C)[n]$, using $\theta$ and the termwise shift identity, are the identity on the only surviving summand $C^{r+n}\otimes_R L$. Both differentials are $(-1)^n(d_C^{r+n}\otimes1)$. Thus this square commutes for every integer $n$, including negative $n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] the shift comparison of $\chi$ is the localization of this total-tensor comparison; by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] that of $\varphi$ is the localization of the termwise identity. Inserting the formula for $a_C$ from step 5 proves the shift square for $\eta_L$ after precomposition with $Q$. Faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] proves the square on $D(R)$. This makes $\eta_L$ an isomorphism of exact functors with their specified shift structures.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YU; derived.tex Tags 014X and 015F

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$, naturality of $\eta_L$ gives commutation with its first two arrows and with $w$ as a map to $X[1]$. Compose the latter naturality square with the shift square from step 6 to obtain commutation with the connecting maps $FZ\to FX[1]$ and $D(T_L)Z\to D(T_L)X[1]$. Both image triangles are distinguished because the two functors are exact. This is precisely the compatibility with all three arrows of the triangle, with no additional choice of cone or sign.

source.place: Tag 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), including the following paragraph defining compatible natural transformations

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$. Apply $H^i$ to $\varphi_C\circ\eta_{L,QC}=Q(\theta_C)\circ\chi_C$, and then compose with $c_C^i$ of step 3 from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Using $H^i(QC)=H^i(C)$ from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives a natural isomorphism on complexes from $H^i(F(QC))$ to $H^i(C)\otimes_R L$. These are the restrictions of the two functors $K\mapsto H^i(FK)$ and $K\mapsto H^i(K)\otimes_R L$ on $D(R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] the comparison and its inverse extend uniquely to these functors on $D(R)$, giving the stated cohomology isomorphism. Its value on every $QC$ is exactly the normalized representative comparison followed by the cycle-and-boundary comparison, since that is the family just extended. All degrees $i$ and all complexes were arbitrary.
